claim: Compares six execution-free predictors in four families (output confidence, EigenScore consistency, hidden-state probe and LAT, causal DAS-based value probe and counterfactual simulation) on Qwen3-Coder-30B and gpt-oss-20b under benchmark shift (LiveCodeBench vs BigCodeBench) and language shift (Python, C++, Java).
stance_target: L2 occupancy: probe versus output confidence on code under shift
scope_conditions: Two models, two benchmarks, three languages; judging prompt returns Yes/No
quoted_support: We compare six execution-free predictors from four families on Qwen3-Coder-30B and gpt-oss-20b under benchmark shift between LiveCodeBench and BigCodeBench and language shift across Python, C++ and Java.

breadth.confidence_families: output Yes/No token probability, EigenScore sampling consistency, linear probe, LAT, DAS value probe, counterfactual simulation (Sec IV)
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present (searched: base, instruct; both models are post-trained)
breadth.reasoning_models: gpt-oss-20b is reasoning but reasoning disabled via final-channel prefill (Sec V-A)
breadth.elicitation_formats: single-token Yes/No judging prompt (Sec III-A); no verbalized numeric confidence (searched: verbalized)
breadth.benchmarks: LiveCodeBench release_v6, BigCodeBench, LCB-Python/C++/Java (Sec V-A, Table I)
breadth.label_independence: verdict labels from the same model's own judgments vs execution (Sec III-B)
breadth.contamination_split: LCB problems released Oct 2024-May 2025 for language shift (Sec V-A); problem-level 60/20/20 splits; no model-cutoff-based split stated
breadth.calibration_metrics: AUROC pooled and within-problem; paired problem-clustered bootstrap (Sec V-C); no ECE
breadth.causal_intervention: yes: DAS interchange interventions, subspace k=6, B=16 bases (Sec IV-D, Eq. 1-3)

claim: For Qwen3-Coder verdict correctness, a probe on the causally localized subspace stays 0.09 AUROC ahead of output confidence under language shift (0.11 in distribution), but this does not generalize consistently to gpt-oss or benchmark shift.
stance_target: L2 partially occupied for probe-beats-confidence under shift
quoted_support: For Qwen3-Coder a probe on the causally localized subspace stays 0.09 AUROC ahead of output confidence under language shift (0.11 in distribution), significantly outperforming the best non-causal predictor by 0.04 AUROC on average.

claim: Program-correctness predictors transfer between benchmarks largely by identifying difficult problems; within-problem ranking is limited and sample-agreement (EigenScore) gives no consistent advantage over a single pass.
stance_target: Pooled AUROC conflates problem-level difficulty and within-problem ranking
quoted_support: For program correctness, predictors transfer more successfully between benchmarks, largely by identifying problems on which the model tends to fail. However, their ability to rank candidates within the same problem is limited.
